# Extract clean titles from first user_query of each relevant transcript
python -c "
import json, re, pathlib
base = pathlib.Path(r'C:\Users\pho\.cursor\projects\c-Users-pho-repos-VSCode-Extensions-vscode-jupyter-cell-tags\agent-transcripts')
uuids = [
  '5febceda-00b7-486b-9df8-4dd63eae36a2',
  'e1cdafed-d82f-452c-bde5-e0ac3c7d372a',
  'ea6532c8-d12a-474b-b2a5-bbd83f3b95bd',
  'd302b768-dd1b-4c21-8cd8-415a456c63d3',
  '427d0728-ce6e-4a54-9a06-caf6a1335416',
]
for u in uuids:
    p = base/u/f'{u}.jsonl'
    if not p.exists():
        print(u, 'MISSING'); continue
    with p.open(encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for line in f:
            o = json.loads(line)
            if o.get('role')!='user': continue
            text = o['message']['content'][0].get('text','')
            m = re.search(r'<user_query>\s*(.*?)\s*</user_query>', text, re.S)
            q = (m.group(1) if m else text)[:180].replace('\n',' ')
            print(f'{u}\n  {q}\n')
            break
"

## Primary transcript (external kernels / VSIX / EH restart)

**[VSIX update without kernel loss](5febceda-00b7-486b-9df8-4dd63eae36a2)**  
User asked (2026-10-13): best way to update via `.VSIX` without reloading the window/notebook and losing kernel state.

### Key quotes / design decisions

1. **No single-extension reload after VSIX**  
   > “There is no official ‘reload only my extension’ path after a VSIX install. VS Code loads extensions into the Extension Host; new code is applied by restarting that host (or the whole window).”

2. **Dev iteration: Restart Extension Host, not Reload Window**  
   > “After compile, use **Developer: Restart Extension Host** instead of **Reload Window**.”  
   > “Keeps the workbench and open notebooks” / “Still restarts *all* extensions (including Jupyter)” / “Local kernels are often disrupted; remote/existing servers fare better.”

3. **After VSIX: Restart Extensions (EH only)**  
   > “Prefer that button / **Developer: Restart Extension Host**”  
   > “Avoid **Developer: Reload Window** unless something fails to reattach”  
   > “Notebook UI usually stays; Jupyter still deactivates/reactivates with the host”  
   > “VS Code even tends to block *auto* EH restart when notebooks/kernels are active”

4. **Best way to keep kernel state: external kernel**  
   > “If preserving variables/session is the real goal, make the kernel outlive VS Code’s Extension Host:”  
   > 1) Start Jupyter outside VS Code (or remote/existing kernel)  
   > 2) **Select Kernel → Existing Jupyter Server…**  
   > 3) Install VSIX / restart extensions  
   > “The server process keeps running; Jupyter reconnects. Local ‘start kernel for me’ sessions usually do **not** survive EH restart cleanly.”

5. **What won’t work**  
   > “Assuming Restart Extensions always preserves a local Jupyter kernel — it often won’t”  
   > Per-extension VSIX hot-swap: not supported

6. **Recommended matrix**  
   - VSIX + keep UI → Restart Extensions  
   - VSIX + keep variables → external/existing Jupyter server + Restart Extensions  
   - Day-to-day → F5 / Extension Development Host (optional self-reload of *your* extension only)
